$comment: Tunisian Derja → Modern Standard Arabic mapping: the `dialect_map` stage of normalization.json.
POLICY (docs/06 §7). Derja is an INPUT language only. It is understood, normalised to MSA and used
to retrieve; it is never emitted. Answers are always MSA or professional Arabic, and never Derja
for religious content — a customer asking a Sharia question in Derja receives an answer in the
language of the reviewed knowledge base, not the language of the street.
TWO LISTS, BECAUSE derja_msa_map IS A MAPPING TABLE.
`mappings`         derjaAr != msa. Seeded into derja_msa_map by V903__seed_derja.sql.
`sharedVocabulary` derjaAr == msa. Tunisian speech and MSA share the word, so there is nothing to
map. NOT seeded — an identity row is noise in a mapping table and makes the
coverage number meaningless — but recorded so the backoffice mining screen
suppresses these instead of proposing them forever.
ALIGNMENT. Each entry carries exactly the columns of derja_msa_map (specs/db/schema.sql) in
camelCase, so the seed migration is a projection of this file and tools/i18n-lint can check one
against the other. `derjaAr` is the table's UNIQUE key: one MSA target per Derja surface form.
That constraint has teeth. During authoring it silently swallowed the domain-critical
وقف = endowment sense, because a verb entry claimed the key first and the dedupe kept the first
occurrence. The verb is now written وقّف with a shadda, and collisions are reported rather than
dropped quietly — see the builder note and the i18n-lint check on duplicate keys.
`category` and `note` have no column: they are authoring metadata. `category` drives the coverage
check; `note` is mandatory for any entry below 0.80 confidence, because a low-confidence mapping
without a written reason is a guess that outlives whoever made it.
GROWTH. This seed set is the floor, not the ceiling. The backoffice proposes new mappings from
Derja queries that went unanswered or retrieved badly; each lands as source=MINED, status=REJECTED
until a reviewer accepts it (docs/06 §7, docs/09).

policy.homographRule: A Derja form whose two senses are both frequent is NOT mapped blindly. Either it is already valid MSA and belongs in sharedVocabulary (عام، قريب، دين as religion), or it is mapped with contextRequired=true and a written contextWhen predicate that the retriever must satisfy first. A confidence float alone cannot express 'only in a fiscal context' — and a map that rewrites القطاع العام into القطاع سنة is worse than no map.
policy.contextRequiredMeans: the runtime applies this entry only when contextWhen holds; i18n-lint requires a note and caps confidence at 0.80
policy.seedTargetCounts: mappings only; sharedVocabulary entries are not mappings and do not count
policy.growth: backoffice proposes mappings from unanswered or mis-retrieved Derja queries; source=MINED, status=REJECTED until reviewed

$comment: Latin-script Derja is transliterated before language detection (normalization.json stage
`arabizi_transliterate`). `derjaLatin` here is the single canonical spelling per term:
derja_msa_map has one latin column and derja_ar is unique, so spelling variants
(chnowa / chnouwa) are folded by the transliteration stage rather than stored as separate rows.
A row per spelling would violate the UNIQUE constraint or tempt someone to relax it.

categories.interrogative: question words — the highest-value class, because a Derja question that is not understood is a question that is not answered
categories.noun: everyday nouns, documents, loans and administrative vocabulary
categories.finance: banking and finance vocabulary, including French loans in daily Tunisian use
categories.sharia: religious and Islamic-finance vocabulary — mapped conservatively, because a wrong rewrite here is a governance incident, not a recall miss

mappings.note: Homograph with literally 'walking'.

mappings.contextWhen: followed by a negated or expected event
mappings.note: Homograph with 'still'.
Written with the shadda. Without it the entry claims the key of the noun حل = solution and silently deletes it — the same trap that ate وقف = endowment.
Tunisian سدّ = to close. The MSA reading 'dam/barrier' is a noun and never a verb here.
Written with the shadda so it cannot claim the key of وقف = endowment (waqf), which is domain-critical.
Both 'read' and 'study'; the study sense dominates in Tunisian speech.

mappings.contextWhen: followed by a place or a time complement
mappings.note: Also 'he exceeded'; the crossing reading dominates with a place complement.
Domain-relevant: Ijara financing conversations start here.
Tunisian بيت = room, not 'house' as in other dialects; getting this wrong inverts a property question.

mappings.contextWhen: never applied to a property-finance question
mappings.note: Regional homograph: 'house' in the south, 'courtyard' in Tunis.
Ubiquitous in Tunisian banking speech: 'دوسي القرض' is how customers say 'loan file'.

mappings.contextWhen: query is not about a generic document upload
mappings.note: From French 'police'. In a banking conversation it is an insurance policy, not a generic document — the generic reading would lose the insurance intent.
Frequently financed; distinct from عرس = the marriage itself.
False friend: Tunisian 'كار' is a bus, never a car.
Agricultural speech; relevant to seasonal financing.

mappings.contextWhen: query mentions a cheque or a card
mappings.note: Homograph: Tunisian banking usage from French 'faire opposition' versus political opposition.
From Italian settimana.

mappings.contextWhen: query mentions a tariff, a fee or a document stamp
mappings.note: Homograph: Tunisian 'fee' (معلوم الطابع، معلوم الشهر) versus MSA 'known'.

mappings.contextWhen: query is fiscal (VAT, tax ID, stamp duty)
mappings.note: Homograph: 'tax' in Tunisian administrative speech (الأداء على القيمة المضافة) versus 'performance' in MSA. The target is qualified so the fiscal sense cannot be confused with the general one.
French loan for both PIN and code; رقم سري is the precise entry for a card PIN.
Rendered as تمويل rather than قرض: the bank sells goods and services, it does not lend money.
Written with the article so it cannot claim the key of جاب = he brought.
Ijara-adjacent vocabulary; the glossary, not this map, decides the product term.
A congratulatory formula, not a literal 'with health'.
docs/06 §7 canonical reading; docs/03 §8 lists لـ, which loses the purposive sense.
Homograph: also the past tense of 'to be'. Blindly rewriting كان البنك مفتوحا to إذا البنك مفتوحا would corrupt a factual question.
Calque of French 'en ligne'.

mappings.contextWhen: query is a duration question, not a date question
mappings.note: Homograph with Friday. Duration questions dominate in banking chat, but a date question must keep the surface form or a Friday appointment becomes a week.

mappings.contextWhen: intent is financial and not SHARIA_CONCEPT
mappings.note: Homograph with دِين = religion. The mapping is written with a fatha on the د so the target is unambiguous, and it is applied only in a financial context — never for a SHARIA_CONCEPT intent.
The single highest-frequency Derja function word; without it a relative clause never matches an MSA document.
Also 'good'; the comparative reading appears with من.
Literally 'his head'; the reflexive sense is the common one.

sharedVocabulary.note: Two senses share the spelling: the noun (a municipal extract, مضمون ولادة) and the adjective ('guaranteed'). The noun takes the key because it is the one that appears in a documents checklist; the adjective is already valid MSA and needs no mapping.
Homograph: 'investment' in finance, 'recruitment' in HR. Kept as an identity entry — the intent classifier decides, not a string map.
Colloquially 'bank branch'; the glossary disambiguates against فرع rather than this map.
Domain-critical. The verb 'to stop' is written وقّف with a shadda precisely so it cannot claim this key.
Noun reading. The verb 'to open' is حلّ in Derja and is a separate entry; this one is the noun.
Flagged sharia-sensitive in term_glossary; the assistant never presents interest as a product feature.

NOT MAPPED: قريب is already valid MSA as an adjective ('near') and as an adverb ('almost'). Rewriting قريب من الوكالة into تقريبا من الوكالة would corrupt a branch-locator question, and nothing is gained — the surface form is identical.

NOT MAPPED: عام is already valid MSA for both 'year' and 'general', so there is nothing to normalise. Mapping it to سنة would rewrite القطاع العام into nonsense — a homograph whose two senses are both frequent belongs to the intent layer, not to a blind string map.
